title: Optimization of Mechanical Properties of Cr3C2-Ni20Cr/Graphite Cold Sprayed Coatings
InformationInFigures: Yes. Could maybe see grain size in Fig. 5 and 6.

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: Cr3C2 have an irregular shape with angular edges and are porous, while Ni20Cr is spherical, oval, elongated shape, and is smaller than Cr3C2 and not porous. For the Ni-25Graphite powder, they are irregular in shape, and the nickel is an even, thin shell around the graphite grains with a thickness of 3-6 μm and up to 10 μm.
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Particle_Size_Other: Ni-25Graphite has a d10 of 47.2 μm, d50 of 80.8 μm, and d90 of 138.9 μm. The Diamalloy 3004 values are d10 of 7.5 μm, d50 of 19.9 μm and d90 of 45.6 μm.
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: cleaned with acetone and grit-blasted using size 30 corundum

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: For cross-section analysis, both powders and coatings were embedded in a resin and were successively polished by diamond suspensions of the gradations 3, 1, and 0.25 µm. Powder blends were mixed for one hour.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: 22.83 ± 0.58 vol% Cr3C2 in coating. 1.10 ± 0.31 vol% graphite in coating. No porosity. Ni20Cr grains are highly deformed. Cr3C2 grains are crushed and jammed in the substrate and matrix. grain size is much smaller than powder size, due to crumbling. Graphite also easily deformed, as it filled all spaces of unevenness, and increased graphite resulted in increased dustiness. The nickel was visible on more weakly deformed graphite grains and the thickness was decreased to 0.5 μm to several microns, and is found in the coating as long stripes.

Experiments.Notes: Experiment 1. A majority of the paper was capturing the S/N ratios of parameters affecting the deposits using the taguchi method. it was noted that the most important parameter influencing the chromium carbide content in the coating is gas composition, the contribution of which is 93.8%. A similar value of 93% is the contribution of the amount of graphite in the powder mixture to the content of the deposition, and it also contributed 89.2% to coating hardness. For the coefficient of friction, the content of graphite, spraying distance, and gas composition, have a contribution is 30.3%, 28.6%, and 23.4%, respectively. The contribution of the traverse gun speed is the smallest and amounts to 17.8%.
